acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p stoa-core -- util tests pass; cargo clippy -p stoa-core clean; is_loopback_addr exists in stoa_core::util and is re-exported; no duplicate in reader/config.rs or transit/config.rs
description:
## What
Move the duplicated is_loopback_addr helper from reader/config.rs and transit/config.rs into crates/core/src/util.rs so mail, smtp, and imap can use it without duplication.

## Algorithm
1. Read crates/core/src/util.rs (may not exist — check lib.rs for existing pub mod util).
2. If util.rs does not exist, create crates/core/src/util.rs and add pub mod util; to lib.rs.
3. Copy the is_loopback_addr(addr: &str) -> bool function from crates/reader/src/config.rs to crates/core/src/util.rs, making it pub.
4. The exact function body: parse the host from addr (split at last ':'), call addr.parse::<IpAddr>().map(|a| a.is_loopback()).unwrap_or(false). Handle '[' prefix for IPv6.
5. In crates/reader/src/config.rs: remove the local is_loopback_addr and replace call sites with stoa_core::util::is_loopback_addr (or add use stoa_core::util::is_loopback_addr).
6. In crates/transit/src/config.rs: same replacement.
7. cargo fmt --all; cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings; cargo test --workspace — all must pass.

## Defensive programming rules
- Parse errors in addr (unparseable host) must return false (treat as non-loopback → more restrictive), never panic.
- No unwrap() without comment explaining it cannot fail.
- No log statements needed — this is a pure utility function.

## Agent team
- Agent R: Read reader/config.rs to get exact function body and all call sites. Read core/src/lib.rs.
- Agent I: Implement the move as described.
- Agent T: Write unit tests for is_loopback_addr in core crate: loopback IPv4 (127.0.0.1:PORT), loopback IPv6 ([::1]:PORT), non-loopback (0.0.0.0:PORT, 192.168.1.1:PORT), invalid input (empty string, 'foo'). Expected values derived from IpAddr::is_loopback() spec, not from the implementation.

## Tests
- test_loopback_ipv4: is_loopback_addr('127.0.0.1:9090') == true. Oracle: RFC 5735 §3 defines 127.0.0.0/8 as loopback.
- test_loopback_ipv6: is_loopback_addr('[::1]:9090') == true. Oracle: RFC 4291 §2.5.3 defines ::1 as loopback.
- test_non_loopback_any: is_loopback_addr('0.0.0.0:9090') == false. Oracle: 0.0.0.0 is not in 127.0.0.0/8.
- test_non_loopback_private: is_loopback_addr('192.168.1.1:1119') == false. Oracle: private range, not loopback.
- test_parse_error: is_loopback_addr('not-an-addr') == false. Oracle: fail-safe default.
title: core: add shared is_loopback_addr to stoa_core::util
